primitives.name: Free Kick Positional Requirement
primitives.verbatim_quote: (a) The side which has a free-kick must be behind the ball when it is kicked.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes a defined kicking direction and a flat playing field.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down if the kicker violates the 'behind the ball' rule, resulting in a re-kick.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's conformal prediction regions for legal kicking zones, ensuring adversarial robustness against spatial overreach.
layer2.telemetry: Measures the lateral offset of the kicker relative to the ball's centerline at the moment of contact.

primitives.name: Minimum Distance Requirement
primitives.verbatim_quote: NOTL—Othcraise the kick must be made again under conditions laid down in Penalties—H.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes a fixed yardage threshold (10 yards) and a non-stop trajectory.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails if the ball stops prematurely due to opponent interference or ground contact before reaching the threshold.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's state-transition logic where a failed minimum distance triggers a reset state, preventing progression to next phase.
layer2.telemetry: Records the actual distance traveled by the ball upon release, compared against the 10-yard baseline.

primitives.name: Fall-on Strategy
primitives.verbatim_quote: SuGGESTioN.—In case a short kick is made by your side on a kick-off, kick-out or kick from a fair catch, and the ball does not go ten yards, fall on it.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes that the kicker can reach the ball before the opponent secures possession.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down if the opponent wins the scramble for the loose ball, converting a re-kick opportunity into live-ball possession.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's optimal stopping theory, balancing the probability of recovering the ball versus the risk of giving up field position.
layer2.telemetry: Tracks the time-to-contact between the kicker and the ball, contrasting it with the opponent's equivalent metric.

primitives.name: Charging Lawfulness
primitives.verbatim_quote: (a) Charging is lawful, in case of a punt-out or kick-off, as soon as the ball is kicked; and the opponents must not charge until the ball is kicked.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes synchronized timing between the kick and the charging action, ignoring reaction delays.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down if defenders violate the 'wait-for-the-kick' rule, leading to illegal contact penalties.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's temporal reasoning framework, enforcing a hard causal ordering constraint on defender engagement events.
layer2.telemetry: Logs the exact timestamp of the ball's release versus the first defender's forward movement.
